title: Ep 1: Hello World, pg_bio! The Central Dogma in SQL
subtitle: DNA -> RNA -> Protein Physics & 1D Genomic Safe Harbors (int4range GiST)
bio_problem: Biology's Central Dogma compiles 4 DNA bases (A, T, G, C) into 20 amino acids. When inserting synthetic genes via CRISPR, you must find a Safe Harbor near a tissue promoter without intersecting tumor suppressor genes, then verify the protein's charge (pI) and hydropathy.
cs_mechanism: PostgreSQL 1D int4range GiST overlap (&&) and distance (<->) operators scan billions of base pairs, while single-pass Rust byte slices compute bio_translate_dna(), isoelectric_point(), and gravy_score() in 200 ns.
speedup: 200x faster than BioPython (~200 ns/protein in Rust)
bullets: • Hydropathy (GRAVY) & Shannon Entropy in a single byte pass
rosetta_mappings: 1D spatial interval tree with O(log N) overlap & nearest-neighbor operators
Finds CRISPR genomic Safe Harbors near promoters while avoiding oncogenes
Zero-allocation 3-byte ASCII codon slice -> amino acid byte stream
Translates raw genomic DNA reading frames into functional protein sequences
Predicts whether an enzyme stays soluble or precipitates in acid/salt vats
narrations: Hello World, and welcome to Episode 1 of pg_bio! If you are a software or database engineer, biology can look like a wall of jargon. But the Central Dogma of biology is literally a compiler: DNA is 4-letter source code on disk, RNA is an ephemeral message queue, and proteins are compiled 3D state machines.

In traditional bioinformatics, engineers export gigabytes of FASTA and VCF files to Python just to translate codons or check genomic intervals. With pg_bio, that entire compiler runs natively inside PostgreSQL shared buffers in Rust.

Here is your first Systems-to-Biotech bridge: a human chromosome is just a 1D integer coordinate space. Using PostgreSQL int4range and GiST indexes, finding a CRISPR safe-harbor locus near a promoter without touching a tumor suppressor gene is a sub-millisecond interval query.

Look at psql: in one query, bio_translate_dna compiles DNA codons into amino acids, isoelectric_point runs 100-step Henderson-Hasselbalch bisection to find net charge, and gravy_score measures water-repellency in 200 nanoseconds.
You just executed genomics and protein sequence physics in 0.2 milliseconds inside SQL. Explore all articles at ideia dot me and check out the pg_bio repository on GitHub.
